phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Analysis of gas cap consistency between txpool admission and block validation reveals a potential trust boundary integrity issue. The system uses a single configuration value (DefaultBuilderGasLimit = 60000000) that is applied to both the execution layer's miner.gaslimit (txpool) and the consensus layer's builder gas limit, but there is no explicit validation that enforces consistency between these two boundaries during runtime.

txpool_domain.transformation: Direct assignment from config to command-line flag

block_validation_domain.transformation: Wrapped in validator.Uint64 with reviewGasLimit function

validation_points.txpool_validation: None found - geth client accepts miner.gaslimit flag without cross-validation
validation_points.block_validation: target_workspace/beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go:ProcessPayload - validates timestamp, randao, parent_hash but NOT gas_limit
validation_points.payload_header_storage: Lines 203-209 in payload.go show gas_limit is stored in state.latest_execution_payload_header but not validated against txpool limit

scenario_1.description: Config value used consistently at initialization

scenario_2.description: Runtime reconfiguration of proposer settings without EL restart
scenario_2.consensus_risk: High - blocks could be accepted by CL but rejected by EL peers, or vice versa

scenario_3.description: Direct geth flag override without updating Prysm config
scenario_3.consensus_risk: High - transaction pool admits different set than what block validation expects

unbounded_growth_risk.description: reviewGasLimit function (loader.go:256-268) only validates against percentage thresholds but does not enforce upper bound consistency with txpool configuration
unbounded_growth_risk.code_evidence: Lines 149 and 113 in miner.go and node.go show miner.gaslimit set from config, but no runtime check ensures this matches proposer BuilderConfig.GasLimit

null_pointer_risk.description: Config value always has default, reviewGasLimit converts 0 to default

overflow_risk.description: Both use uint64, no overflow possible within type bounds

race_condition_risk.description: Execution layer (geth) and consensus layer (Prysm) can be configured independently, creating window where gas limits diverge without detection

tb-001_txpool_admission.configuration_source: Command-line flag in miner.go:149 and node.go:113

consistency_enforcement.finding: No code found that validates tb-001.gas_cap == tb-003.gas_cap at runtime
consistency_enforcement.impact: Potential consensus divergence if configurations drift

initialization_flow.step_3: Value passed to geth via --miner.gaslimit flag (execution layer)
initialization_flow.step_4: Same value used in config/proposer/loader/loader.go for BuilderConfig.GasLimit (consensus layer)
initialization_flow.abstract_state: Both boundaries initialized to same value from single source

txpool_path.abstract_domain: Set of transactions T where ∀t ∈ T: t.gas <= miner.gaslimit

block_validation_path.entry: Prysm receives execution payload in block
block_validation_path.abstract_domain: Set of payloads P where payload.gas_limit is unrestricted by CL validation

divergence_point.location: Between geth txpool and Prysm payload validation
divergence_point.condition: If miner.gaslimit != BuilderConfig.GasLimit, state spaces diverge

recommended_verification.check_2: Implement runtime assertion that execution layer gas limit matches consensus layer configuration
recommended_verification.check_3: Add integration test that verifies tb-001 and tb-003 use identical gas cap values
recommended_verification.check_4: Document the trust assumption that both layers must be configured consistently
